newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-PET. IPIRANGA SA MAINTAINED.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-PET. IPIRANGA SA MAINTAINED.

text.p: Caspian Securities said Tuesday it has maintained its market-performer rating on Brazilian oil products firm Petroleo Ipiranga after release of the company's second-quarter 1997 financial results.

-- Caspian analysts Eric Graber-Lopez and Daniel Barcelo said in a report the firm's second-quarter earnings of $0.66 per share ($35.01 million), were up 32 percent year-on-year and 49 percent quarter-on-quarter.
-- "While the earnings improvement was very good, we were surprised to see the company's gross margin fall versus previous quarters," they wrote.
-- The higher earnings were due to operating improvements and lower taxes as well as administrative cost reductions, they added.
-- "We believe the company's long-term outlook is quite positive now that Brazil's oil sector has been deregulated, allowing the company to backwardly integrate its operations," they wrote.

-- But integration will not occur in the short term as the ANP watchdog will regulate transactions in the refining sector and a five-year transition period will prevent any major changes in the sector's structure, they added.
-- Petroleo Ipiranga preferred was flat at 20.50 reais at 1233 local/1533 GMT in Sao Paulo.
